items.title: Public Preview: Azure ExpressRoute resiliency guard
items.description:
Azure ExpressRoute resiliency guard is now available in public preview for ExpressRoute virtual network gateways. The new resiliency model property lets you specify whether a gateway is intended for a single-homed or multi-homed configuration, helping align your deployment with the resiliency requirements of your workloads.

For multi-homed gateways, resiliency guard guides you to connect either two ExpressRoute circuits in different peering locations or an ExpressRoute Metro circuit. Portal guidance and configuration safeguards help identify incomplete setups and reduce the risk of changes that could weaken gateway resiliency. Single-homed configurations remain available for workloads that do not require multi-site resiliency. 

Learn more.

items.title: Announcing:  Azure Databricks Genie One and Genie Agents Free Usage extended through January 31, 2027
items.description:
Free usage of Genie One and Genie Agents in Azure Databricks is now extended through January 31, 2027, from the previous end date of July 31, 2026. Budget controls do not apply to these products during the promotional period. The promotion covers usage by users only - service principals are excluded, and their Genie One and Genie Agents usage continues to be billed. Genie Code is not included in this promotion: each Genie Code user continues to receive 150 free Databricks units (DBUs) per month, and usage above that allowance receives a 25% promotional discount through January 31, 2027, combined with applicable discounts on the Serverless Real-Time Inference SKU. 

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Migrate from AWS FSx for Windows File Server to Azure Files with Azure Storage Mover
items.description:
Azure Storage Mover now supports agentless, cloud-to-cloud migration from AWS FSx for Windows File Server (SMB) to Azure Files (SMB), in preview. You can move your Windows file shares off FSx and into Azure Files without deploying or managing a migration agent — the service handles the transfer for you. File data is copied directly from FSx to your Azure file share over a private connection between Azure and your AWS network.

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: SharePoint Connector for Azure Databricks
items.description:
The SharePoint connector for Azure Databricks is now generally available. Organizations can use Lakeflow Connect to ingest files from SharePoint into Azure Databricks, helping unify enterprise content with data and AI workflows on Azure. The connector supports incremental ingestion, Unity Catalog governance, and multiple authentication methods for enterprise-scale deployments.  

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Unity AI Gateway on Azure Databricks
items.description:
Unity AI Gateway is now generally available on Azure Databricks. Unity AI Gateway provides centralized governance for AI models, agents, tools, and MCP services, helping organizations monitor usage, manage costs, apply guardrails, and enforce access controls across AI workloads. Built on Unity Catalog, it extends governance capabilities across both Azure Databricks and external AI services.  

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Explicit proxy in Azure Firewall
items.description:
Azure Firewall explicit proxy is now generally available. Explicit proxy enables customers to configure applications and browsers to send HTTP and HTTPS traffic directly to Azure Firewall using proxy settings, providing an alternative to route-based traffic steering and enabling more granular control over outbound web traffic. 

The GA release builds on extensive customer validation during public preview, where explicit proxy was enabled across 300+ Azure subscriptions and adopted by approximately 40 S500 customers. Customer feedback gathered during preview directly influenced several key enhancements delivered as part of GA, including support for serving both HTTP and HTTPS destinations through a single proxy endpoint, Managed Identity-based PAC file retrieval, and an improved portal configuration experience. 

A key customer use case for explicit proxy is Azure Arc onboarding in hybrid environments. Organizations can use Azure Firewall as a forward proxy for Arc-enabled servers, enabling secure connectivity to required Microsoft services while maintaining centralized outbound access controls. Combined with support for forward proxy migration scenarios and application-level traffic steering, Explicit Proxy helps customers simplify network operations while leveraging Azure Firewall's existing security capabilities. 

Learn more.

items.title: Retirement: Nested confidential (cc_v5) VMs will be retired on September 1, 2026
items.description: On September 1, 2026, the cc_v5 confidential VM series will be retired and will no longer be available for use or purchase. Any affected VM that has not been resized before that date will deallocated. The impacted VM sizes that will be retired are: DCas_cc_v5, DCads_cc_v5, ECas_cc_v5, and ECads_cc_v5.

items.title: Public Preview: Perimeter link feature in network security perimeter
items.description:
Perimeter link (cross-perimeter connectivity) is a network security perimeter capability that allows trusted resources in two different network security perimeters to securely communicate with each other using Managed Identity (MSI), without requiring additional network security perimeter access rules or network configuration changes. It preserves Zero Trust boundaries while enabling controlled service-to-service access across perimeters 

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Azure Private Link support over IPv6
items.description:
Azure Private Link over IPv6 enables you to privately access Azure PaaS services, such as Azure Storage and Azure SQL Database, over IPv6-based connectivity. You can now use IPv6 private endpoints to connect from IPv6 clients in an Azure virtual network or from on-premises networks over ExpressRoute. 

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Azure DNS enables DNS-based load balancing through Traffic Manager integration
items.description:
Azure DNS now offers a seamless way to integrate with Azure Traffic Manager for DNS-based traffic routing. Customers can now directly associate Azure DNS record set with Traffic Manager profiles without creating CNAME record for trafficmanager.net domain. This improves lookup latency by eliminating a CNAME hop and enables DNSSEC compatibility for load balanced records by removing unsigned trafficmanager.net domain from CNAME lookup chain.

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Azure Virtual Network routing appliance
items.description:
Azure Virtual Network routing appliance is now generally available. It delivers private connectivity across virtual networks, using specialized hardware for low latency, high throughput, and better performance than virtual machines. 

Key benefits and functionalities: 

  • High-bandwidth east-west routing: provisioned bandwidth tiers up to 200 Gbps per instance.  
  • Dual-stack and IPv6 at scale: IPv4, IPv6, and dual-stack virtual networks, including IPv6 access control list enforcement.  
  • Scale-out private access: global and cross-region private endpoint support through a single appliance.  
  • No operational overhead: fully managed with built-in high availability and availability zone resiliency.  
  • Built-in monitoring: throughput, packet, and flow metrics available in Azure Monitor with no diagnostic configuration required. 
Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Trusted Launch as Default
items.description:
Trusted Launch as Default (TLaD) is now generally available for new Azure Gen2 virtual machines and virtual machine scale sets. TLaD automatically enables Secure Boot and vTPM for supported deployments, helping customers establish a stronger security baseline for workloads at no additional cost.

New Gen2 VMs deployed through Azure Portal, Azure CLI, and Azure PowerShell automatically use Trusted Launch by default. Customers deploying through ARM templates, Bicep, Terraform, and Azure SDKs can extend the same experience with a one-time subscription registration. Existing VMs remain unchanged, and any explicitly configured security settings continue to be honored.

Trusted Launch is available on supported x64 and Arm64 Gen2 VM sizes across Azure public, Azure Government, and Azure China regions.

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Immutability to the most recent seven days of backups on Azure SQL Database and Azure SQL Managed Instance
items.description:
To enhance backup protection, Azure SQL Database and Azure SQL Managed Instance now automatically apply immutability to the most recent seven days of backups. This capability is enabled by default for all databases, regardless of the configured point-in-time restore retention period. No action or configuration is required.

Note: Support for Azure SQL Hyperscale backups is coming in a future release.

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Single-click purchase for public SaaS offers
items.description:
Eligible SaaS products on Microsoft Marketplace now support a simplified purchase experience in Azure portal. Customers can review plan, billing, resource group, contact details, and terms information on a single page for completing the purchase. This experience isn’t currently supported for SaaS offers that use a custom purchasing experience (i.e. Azure native integrations, Model-as-a-Service, Secure Exchange products, etc.).

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Route-Maps for Azure Route Server
items.description:
Route maps for Azure Route Server are now available in public preview, providing fine-grained control over inbound and outbound routing across hybrid connections. Customers can manage routes advertised to and from Azure Route Server BGP peerings with Network Virtual Appliances (NVAs), ExpressRoute gateways, and VPN gateways in the same virtual network. Route-maps provide the following capabilities: 

  • Route summarization: Summarize routes when on-premises networks connect to the virtual network through ExpressRoute or VPN. 
  • Route control: Control routes entering and leaving Azure Route Server between on-premises networks, NVAs, and virtual networks. 
  • Path selection: Modify BGP attributes such as AS-PATH to make routes more or less preferred. 
  • Route tagging: Tag routes by using the BGP Community attribute. 

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Azure SQL updates for late-July
items.description:
In late-July 2026, the following update and enhancement was made to Azure SQL: 

  • Regex-based dynamic data masking (DDM) extends the built-in DDM feature with pattern‑based masking to hide sensitive data like emails, phone numbers, and identifiers—centrally enforced at the database layer.

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Azure Database for PostgreSQL flexible server in India South Central
items.description:
Now you can deploy Azure Database for PostgreSQL flexible server in the India South Central Azure region.   

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Azure Automation supports PowerShell 7.6 runbooks and Runtime environment
items.description:
Azure Automation is pleased to announce: 
  • General Availability of in-support PowerShell 7.6  runbooks
  • Runtime Environment GA, enabling customers to seamlessly upgrade their outdated scripts to supported runtime versions.  
  • Support for Azure CLI commands in PowerShell 7.6 runbooks GA 

Benefits: 

  • Stay current – Access to new language versions for improved security and performance. 
  • Faster Runbook upgrade – Easy portability of runbooks across different versions to keep pace with PowerShell and Python releases. 
  • Granular control – Complete control to configure the script execution environment, without worrying about conflicting module versions. 
  • Efficient Code organization – Eliminate the need to create multiple Automation accounts to segregate different versions of modules or conflicting modules. 

Learn more: 

  • Azure Automation runbook types | Microsoft Learn  
  • Upgrade runbook to latest language version  
  • Create PowerShell runbooks with Azure CLI commands  
  • Language runtime support and retirement policy for Azure Automation | Microsoft Learn

items.title: Announcing: Reservation exchanges for Azure services supported by savings plans will no longer be available starting February 1, 2027
items.description:
Starting February 1, 2027, Azure reservations exchanges will no longer be available for services covered by savings plans.  At the time of this announcement, this includes reservations for the following services:    

  • Compute services: Azure Virtual Machines, including exchanges between non-premium and premium storage, Azure Dedicated Host, and Azure App Service. 

  • Database services: Azure Database for PostgreSQL, Azure Database for MySQL, Azure DocumentDB, Azure Cosmos DB, Azure SQL Database, and Azure SQL Managed Instance.  

Each active reservation for impacted services purchased before February 1, 2027, will retain the right to one final exchange after that date.  

This reservation exchange policy update excludes products or services that are deprecated and approaching end of life, as well as cloud environments that don’t currently support savings plans. 

As savings plans coverage expands, reservations for those services will follow this policy and will not support exchanges. 

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Symmetric keys on Azure Key Vault Premium
items.description:
We’re announcing symmetric keys on Azure Key Vault Premium are now available in public preview. 

This preview enables customers and partners to evaluate symmetric encryption capabilities using the oct-HSM key type and the Advanced Encryption Standard (AES) algorithm directly within Azure Key Vault. Customers can use AES algorithms to encrypt, decrypt, wrap, and unwrap data while continuing to benefit from Azure-managed security, compliance, and operational controls. 

AES algorithms with 256-bit keys are aligned with CNSA 2.0 requirements and can help organizations prepare for post-quantum cryptography readiness scenarios. 

Key benefits include: 

  • Centralized key management through Azure Key Vault Premium 
  • Support for oct-HSM symmetric keys 
  • AES-based encryption and decryption operations 
  • Simplified integration with existing Azure security workflows 
  • Consistent security and operational controls across Azure services 

Note: Azure portal support for symmetric key management is currently rolling out. During the rollout period, customers can use Azure CLI, ARM templates to create and manage oct-HSM symmetric keys and access the full preview functionality. 

Learn more:

  • About keys  
  • Key types, algorithms, and operations

items.title: Public Preview: Support for SMB Opportunistic Locking (Oplocks) configuration
items.description:
Azure NetApp Files now supports configuration of SMB opportunistic locking (oplocks) for SMB and dual-protocol volumes. Opportunistic locks (Oplocks) improve SMB client caching and are enabled by default. You can configure oplocks on new volumes or update the setting on existing volumes. System default is the default selection and enables opportunistic locks on the volume. A cross-region replication destination volume can use an oplock setting independent of its source volume. 

Learn more:

  • Create an SMB volume for Azure NetApp Files | Microsoft Learn  
  • Create a dual-protocol volume for Azure NetApp Files | Microsoft Learn 
  • What is Azure NetApp Files | Microsoft Learn

items.title: Public Preview: Azure Monitor Logs mirroring into Microsoft Fabric
items.description:
This capability shares telemetry from Azure Monitor Log Analytics workspaces into Microsoft Fabric, making observability data available in OneLake as Delta Parquet, the open format, without duplication and with near real-time availability. All Azure Monitor Logs tiers are supported, including Analytics, Basic, and Auxiliary logs.

Once available in Fabric, Azure Monitor data can be analyzed alongside operational and business data using Fabric capabilities such as Eventhouse, Power BI, Spark.

What you can do:
Organizations can combine telemetry with business context from systems such as ERP and CRM to gain deeper insight into the business impact of operational events, supporting cross-domain analysis, more informed decision-making, and faster action. Organizations can also apply advanced analytics, machine learning, long-term trend analysis, and reporting directly to their observability data.

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Azure Sphere OS version 26.09 is now available for evaluation
items.description:
Azure Sphere OS version 26.09 RC1 is now available for evaluation in the Retail Eval feed. Whilst this release encompasses no customer-facing changes, it represents a major bump in Azure Sphere's underlying Linux kernel version as part of our long-term support and security commitment, as such, this release will operate for an extended evaluation period, until September 2026, enabling additional time for customer evaluation testing.

Whilst we've taken every measure to ensure that this update does not impact any of our contractual surfaces, with over six months of extensive integration and regression testing, we strongly encourage customers to evaluate this release with their in-market applications and to raise any issues with the Azure Sphere product group as early on as possible.

Following this evaluation period, 26.09 will be promoted and deployed broadly to devices in the Retail feed.

The 26.09 RC1 OS Retail Eval release includes a major Linux kernel version bump.

items.title: Public Preview: Azure Enclave
items.description:
Announcing the public preview of Azure Enclave for Microsoft Azure, Azure Government, Azure Government Secret, and Azure Government Top Secret. Azure Enclave helps streamline the deployment and management of isolated cloud environments for sensitive workloads across government and other regulated industries. Azure Enclave helps customers quickly deliver their critical workloads while maintaining essential security and isolation. Azure Enclave is designed to isolate virtual networking infrastructure by default and includes controls intended to help ensure connections are explicitly configured and managed. 

With Azure Enclave, customers can: 

  • Quickly deploy secured environments using managed infrastructure and predefined architectural patterns. 
  • Provide access to authorized users in shared environments with controlled data access policies and defined permissions. 
  • Configure secured connections to sensitive data using endpoints you define and control for connectivity between resources. 
  • Apply multiple security controls, including network segmentation, role-based access, and monitoring, to help protect workloads and simplify management. 
Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: NAT64 on StandardV2 NAT Gateway
items.description:
StandardV2 NAT Gateway now supports NAT64, enabling IPv6 workloads to communicate with IPv4-only internet destinations by translating synthesized outbound IPv6 traffic into IPv4 traffic. NAT64 relies on a DNS64-capable resolver to synthesize IPv6 addresses by embedding the IPv4 address within the NAT64 Well-Known Prefix 64:ff9b::/96 – so client traffic is naturally addressed to NAT64 for translation.

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Application Routing with Gateway API
items.description:
Managing ingress routing while adopting newer Kubernetes standards can require balancing modernization efforts with existing deployments. Application Routing with Gateway API is now generally available on AKS, bringing the Kubernetes Gateway API to ingress management without requiring a service mesh. 

Existing ingress-nginx-based Application Routing remains supported until November, and customers can migrate to the Gateway API-based model at their own pace using the open-source ingress2gateway tool. This enables technical practitioners to adopt a standardized routing model while maintaining a lightweight footprint and supporting a gradual transition from existing ingress configurations.

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Resource placement in Azure Kubernetes Fleet Manager
items.description:
Managing Kubernetes resources across multiple clusters can require significant manual effort to apply updates and maintain consistency. Resource placement in Azure Kubernetes Fleet Manager is now generally available and enables platform and application teams to consistently distribute Kubernetes resources across multiple AKS and Arc-enabled clusters.

This release includes the Resource Placement Kubernetes APIs in v1 and introduces a new Azure portal experience for creating, viewing, and managing placements across a fleet. By using placement policies that select target member clusters based on labels and properties, teams can reduce the effort and risk associated with applying, updating, and tracking resources on a cluster-by-cluster basis.

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Maximum allowed failures for update runs in Azure Kubernetes Fleet Manager
items.description:
In fail-fast update rollouts, a small number of member cluster update failures can halt progress across a broader update deployment. Maximum Allowed Failures for update runs in Azure Kubernetes Fleet Manager, now available in preview, introduces an optional setting that allows update runs to continue when some member cluster updates fail.

Customers can define failure thresholds at either the stage or group level using fixed counts or percentages. This gives platform teams more control over the balance between rollout correctness and continued update progress, enabling more flexible and failure-tolerant update strategies across fleet-managed clusters.

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Prepared Image Specification
items.description:
Organizations running large-scale, AI, GPU, Windows, and other performance-sensitive workloads on AKS often experience longer node startup times because new nodes must repeatedly download container images and perform initialization tasks before workloads can run.

With AKS Prepared Image Specification, now in preview, customers can create preconfigured node images that include required container images and customizations ahead of time, enabling new nodes to start in a ready-to-run state. This helps workloads achieve faster and more predictable scaling, reduce application startup latency, and improve operational efficiency during growth and burst traffic events.

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Microsoft Azure now available from new cloud region in India (India South Central)
items.description: Microsoft announces the opening of its fourth datacenter region in India, India South Central, with campuses in Hyderabad, Telangana. The region will provide customers with local, secure, state-of-the-art cloud infrastructure designed with AI readiness as a key focus. It supports growing demand for cloud and AI services, customer digital transformation, local data residency, improved latency, and resilient cloud capacity in India.

items.title: Generally Available: Claude Opus 5 on Azure Databricks
items.description:
Azure Databricks now supports Anthropic Claude Opus 5 through AI Model Serving. Claude Opus 5 is Anthropic's latest model for advanced reasoning, coding, agentic workflows, and professional knowledge work. 

Claude Opus 5 is designed for complex tasks requiring deep reasoning, long-horizon planning, and software development assistance. Customers can use Claude Opus 5 in Azure Databricks to build AI applications and agents on enterprise data.

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: HTTP header insertion in Azure Firewall
items.description:
Azure Firewall now supports HTTP header insertion, enabling organizations to add or overwrite HTTP/HTTPS request headers directly from Azure Firewall application rules. This capability helps customers enforce security controls, support tenant restriction scenarios, integrate with backend services, and simplify application access management without relying on third-party proxies or on-premises infrastructure. 

The feature is especially useful for scenarios such as Microsoft Entra tenant restrictions, Azure Virtual Desktop, VDI, SaaS access control, and enterprise egress filtering. By enabling header insertion natively in Azure Firewall, customers can reduce proxy dependencies, avoid routing traffic back on premises solely for header injection, and improve operational efficiency.  

HTTP header insertion is supported in Azure Firewall Premium for HTTP traffic and HTTPS traffic decrypted using TLS Inspection. In Standard and Basic SKUs, it is supported for HTTP traffic. The feature can be configured through Azure Portal, Azure CLI, PowerShell, REST APIs, Terraform, and Azure Firewall Draft + Deploy. 

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: AI Gateway in Azure API Management
items.description:
The AI Gateway tier for Azure API Management is now available in public preview. Building on the AI gateway capabilities already available across API Management tiers, the new AI Gateway tier provides a dedicated experience optimized for AI workloads.
As organizations operationalize AI, platform teams need a consistent way to securely expose AI assets including AI models, MCP servers, and tools. AI Gateway helps organizations apply consistent security, policies, authentication, observability, and operational controls across AI workloads.

Built on the trusted, enterprise-grade Azure API Management platform, AI Gateway provides portal and programmatic experiences optimized for AI. The experience is centered on models, MCP servers, and tools, making it easier for platform teams to discover, expose, secure, and observe AI assets.

The public preview supports models hosted from Microsoft Foundry as well as models hosted in AWS Bedrock, Google Vertex AI, OpenAI, and Anthropic. It also extends the same consistent controls to MCP servers, created from existing MCP backends, OpenAPI definitions, or connectors, with built-in policy enforcement, OpenTelemetry-based observability, and enterprise authentication.

Learn more: 

  • Announcement blog 
  • Documentation  
  • Build your first AI Gateway resource
